Rules / Correctness

SK2009 An enum switch omits declared members

A switch over a non-flags enum has neither every declared value nor a catch-all arm.

CategoryCorrectness
Default severitywarning
ScopeSemantic
Needs a compilationyes
Runs under --load=looseno
Cached per fileyes
Fixno
Language version floor—
Since2.0

Why

A switch that silently falls through when a new enum member is added turns a closed decision into an accidental default. Listing every value makes the compiler-visible decision explicit and makes future additions show up at the switch that needs a policy.

Example

Instead of:

return color switch { Color.Red => 1, Color.Green => 2 };

Write:

return color switch { Color.Red => 1, Color.Green => 2, Color.Blue => 3 };

When it does not fire

The rule excludes [Flags] enums, whose combinations are intentionally open, and any switch with default, discard, var or declaration catch-all handling. It also skips pattern forms other than constants and or combinations rather than guessing which values a relational, negated or recursive pattern covers. Enum aliases are compared by constant value, so handling one alias handles all aliases with that value. No fix is offered because the correct behavior for a missing value is a domain decision. ⚠ This rule owns the empty `default:` section and `SK0240` stands down for it. The two read the same construct in opposite directions — SK0240 counts a default: that only breaks as dead control flow and offers to delete it — and together they were a fix loop on any enum switch with an empty default. The shared predicate both rules now ask is what keeps "where SK2009 would fire" meaning the same thing in each.

Configuration

  • dotnet_diagnostic.SK2009.severity
